chapter_text_kjv.1: Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
chapter_text_kjv.2: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.
chapter_text_kjv.3: For the Pharisees, and all the Yahudim (Jews), except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.
chapter_text_kjv.4: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.
chapter_text_kjv.5: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?
chapter_text_kjv.6: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Isaiah prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
chapter_text_kjv.7: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
chapter_text_kjv.8: For laying aside the commandment of Elohim (God), ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.
chapter_text_kjv.9: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of Elohim (God), that ye may keep your own tradition.
chapter_text_kjv.10: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
chapter_text_kjv.11: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.
chapter_text_kjv.12: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;
chapter_text_kjv.13: Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.
chapter_text_kjv.14: And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:
chapter_text_kjv.15: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.
chapter_text_kjv.16: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
chapter_text_kjv.17: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
chapter_text_kjv.18: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;
chapter_text_kjv.19: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?
chapter_text_kjv.20: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.
chapter_text_kjv.21: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
chapter_text_kjv.22: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:
chapter_text_kjv.23: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
chapter_text_kjv.24: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
chapter_text_kjv.25: For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:
chapter_text_kjv.26: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.
chapter_text_kjv.27: But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.
chapter_text_kjv.28: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Adonai (Lord): yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.
chapter_text_kjv.29: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.
chapter_text_kjv.30: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.
chapter_text_kjv.31: And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.
chapter_text_kjv.32: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.
chapter_text_kjv.33: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;
chapter_text_kjv.34: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
chapter_text_kjv.35: And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
chapter_text_kjv.36: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it;
chapter_text_kjv.37: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.

threads.title: The corban tradition voids the fifth commandment — Sirach
threads.summary_md: Mark 7:6-13 is the framework's central diagnostic in the King's own mouth: the man-made tradition that voids the commandment of Elohim (God). The corban device is the load-bearing example — *if a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift... he shall be free* — and the verdict is *Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition.* The commandment the device voids is the fifth — *Honour thy father and thy mother* — and the Hebrew library's wisdom-stream had already bound that commandment to the fear of Yahuah and named the cost of withholding it. Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:7 makes honour-of-parents the very test of the fear of Yahuah: *He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father, and will do service to his parents, as to his masters.* Sirach 3:8 binds honour to deed, not word only: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them* — the exact word-AND-deed the corban ruling severs, permitting honour in vow-formula while forbidding the deed of provision. Sirach 3:9 names the cost: *the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.* The tradition that voids the commandment forfeits the blessing and invites the uprooting. The same flesh-credentialing system that exalts the tradition of the elders over the word of Elohim is the Judaizer architecture the King names here and the apostolic letters confront later; the wisdom-stream had already exposed it by its own standard.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:7 — *He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father.* The commandment the corban tradition severs from the fear of Yahuah (God) at Mark 7:10.
Ecclesiasticus 3:8 — *both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* The deed the tradition forbids at Mark 7:12.
Ecclesiasticus 3:9 — *the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children.* The foundation the tradition of Mark 7:13 roots out.

threads.title: Defilement from within — the heart the source of evil in Sirach
threads.summary_md: Mark 7:14-23 turns the washing-of-hands dispute into the King's teaching on the true seat of defilement: *There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man... For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.* The Hebrew library's wisdom-stream had already located the source of evil in the man's own heart, never in what enters from without, and never in Elohim (God). Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15:11-12 forbids blaming the Most High: *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away... Say not you, He has caused me to err: for he has no need of the sinful man.* Sirach 15:14 names why the source is the man's own: *He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel* — the free agent answerable for what proceeds from his own heart. Sirach 27:6 makes the outward utterance the disclosure of the inward heart: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The King's catalogue of what proceeds from within is the same diagnostic the wisdom-stream carried — the heart, not the unwashen hand, is where defilement begins, and what comes out declares the heart that bore it.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15:14 — *He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel.* The Hebrew library locates the source of evil in the man's own choosing; Mark 7:20's *that which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man* names the same.

Sirach 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The outward utterance discloses the inward heart; Mark 7:21's *from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts* is the same diagnostic — the fruit declares the tree.

threads.title: *Ephphatha* — the deaf hearing and the dumb speaking as the messianic-age credential of Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 35
threads.summary_md: *And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain* (Mark 7:35). The crowd's verdict — *he hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak* (Mark 7:37) — is a direct echo of the messianic-age catalog Yeshayahu (Isaiah) gave: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing* (Isaiah 35:5-6). The opening of the ear is the credential the King handed Yochanan's (John's) disciples a chapter earlier in Matthew 11:5 as the answer to *art thou he that should come?* — the answer the prophets had already written down for them to recognize.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: *And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.* The second Aramaic word Mark preserves on the page — the King's own voice spoken over a deaf man, the original word kept so the reader hears what the witnesses heard, the translation given immediately so the meaning is not lost. The same pattern as *Talitha cumi* at 5:41.

*Ephphatha, that is, Be opened. And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.* The ear-opening and tongue-loosing are the messianic-age credentials Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 35:5-6 catalogued: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.*
*And the tongue of the dumb sing.* The King fulfills the catalog the prophet wrote; the dumb-speaking is the second half of the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 35 messianic-age credential.

*The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* The King handed Yochanan's (John's) disciples the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 35 catalog as the answer to *art thou he that should come?* — the Mark 7 ear-opening is the catalog walked into a single moment.

*And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.* The crowd's verdict is also a creation-echo: *and Elohim (God) saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.* The King's healing is creation-restoration; the works of his hands undo the curse on the body the way the original works of his hands made the body.

*He maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak* — the crowd's framework-honoring verdict echoes the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 35:5-6 messianic-age catalog without naming the prophet; the witnesses recognize the substance.

threads.title: The lost sheep first — the woman of Canaan, the divorced house, and the children's bread (Deuteronomy 24; Hosea 2; Mark 7)
threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. A woman cries after him on the coast of Tyre and Sidon, and the disciples want her sent away. His answer is to them, and it tells them who she is:

*But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24)

That was his whole errand. He had given the twelve the same boundary before he ever met her:

*But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6)

And she is not a stranger to the house. Hear what she calls him:

*And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.* (Matthew 15:22)

*Son of David* is the covenant word to David's house in the mouth of a woman on a Canaanite coast. She knew whose house the king came from, and she worshipped him. The sheep hear the voice because they are sheep, and Hosea had already named the place where such sheep would be found:

*Then said Elohim (God), Call his name Lo-ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your Elohim (God).* (Hosea 1:9)

*Yet the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God).* (Hosea 1:10)

So why does he call her a dog, and why is the bread withheld? Because the house she belongs to was put away:

*And I saw, when for all the causes whereby backsliding Yashar'el (Israel) committed adultery I had put her away, and given her a bill of divorce; yet her treacherous sister Yahudah (Judah) feared not, but went and played the harlot also.* (Jeremiah 3:8)

And the Torah he gave does not let a husband take back the wife he has put away:

*Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before Yahuah (LORD): and thou shalt not cause the land to sin, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee for an inheritance.* (Deuteronomy 24:4)

A woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives, and only a death frees her to be married again:

*For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband.* (Romans 7:2)

*Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Messiah (Christ); that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto Elohim (God).* (Romans 7:4)

He has not died yet. The divorced house cannot be seated at his table while he lives as that husband, so the bread is the children's, the undivorced house of Yahudah (Judah), and the scattered are what we became out there, dogs under the table. Mark keeps the word that carries the timing:

*But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.* (Mark 7:27)

First. Not never. She hears the order and does not argue it. She asks for what falls from the table now, and he calls that faith great. The redeeming of the house that was put away comes on the other side of his death, and Hosea says how it ends:

*And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my Elohim (God).* (Hosea 2:23)

The order of the sending shows the same two halves. Before the death, *go not into the way of the Gentiles*; after it:

*Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19)

Not a new people added to the house, but the same house sought in every place it was scattered to, once the death that frees it had been died. Matthew 15 does not say the death is the reason; Deuteronomy, Romans and Mark's *first* say it, line upon line. The woman of Canaan is a woman from that land and a sheep of the house, revealed by her hearing, given the crumbs before her time and the table after it.

threads.title: The gathering of the scattered twelve tribes — Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36, 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13, and Tobit 13 (FRAMEWORK-MAJOR)
threads.summary_md: Matt 15:24's *I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* — the King's-own-mission-scope statement, paired with the Matt 10:5-6's apostolic-mission-scope, reading as the load-bearing scripture-anchor for the framework's gathering-of-the-scattered-twelve-tribes thesis — read against the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the gathering-of-the-scattered-tribes prayer-and-prophecy substance. Five moves: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:1 names the petition — *have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us* (the wisdom-stream's-prayer-for-the-gathering); Sirach 36:11 names THE direct verbal-anchor — *gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (the explicit wisdom-stream-articulation of the twelve-tribes-restoration the prophets had named at Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:21; Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31:8-10; Hosea 1:10-11; Zekharyah (Zechariah) 10:6-10); 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:40 names the ten-tribes-carried-away — *those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive* (the wisdom-stream's-direct-articulation of the Assyrian-exile-architecture the lost-sheep-mission-scope addresses); 2 Esdras 13:48 names the remnant-within-the-borders — *but those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders* (the wisdom-stream's naming of both registers the King's-mission addresses); Tobit 13:5 names the scourge-then-mercy-then-gathering-out-of-all-nations — *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us* (the operative-architecture the King's-mission enacts). The framework reads the cluster as FRAMEWORK-MAJOR for the lost-sheep-mission-scope's wisdom-stream corroboration. The Pharisaic-system had built credentialing-systems on top of the binary (Yahudah (Judah) and the nations, no scattered-twelve-tribes coming-home); the wisdom-stream had preserved the architecture the prophets had named. The King's-mission at v.24 IS the operative-form of the wisdom-stream's-prayer at Sirach 36:11; the lost-sheep-of-the-house-of-Yashar'el (Israel) the King is sent-to IS the all-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob) the wisdom-stream had prayed for the gathering of. The framework reads the Canaanite-woman's mercy-at-the-crumbs-substance (vv.25-28) within the architecture — as the master's-table-mercy-to-the-categorical-nations-individual that does NOT collapse the seed-distinction (Red Line #7) but operates within it.

threads.title: The honor of parents — the fifth-commandment substance the Pharisaic Corban-tradition voids — Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3 and 7, and Tobit 4
threads.summary_md: Matt 15:3-6's Pharisaic-Corban-tradition exposé — *Why do ye also transgress the commandment of Elohim (God) by your tradition? For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother ... But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition* — read against the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the fifth-commandment substance the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition voids. Five moves: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:1 names *hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe* (the wisdom-stream's headline articulation of the parental-honor architecture as the foundation-of-the-children's-safety); Sirach 3:8 names the holistic-honor — *honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them* (the architecture the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition split, allowing word-without-deed); Sirach 7:27 names the whole-heart-honor — *honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother* (the heart-level architecture the King will close the loop on at vv.18-20); Sirach 3:16 names the worst-end — *he that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God)* (the disposition of the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition at its most-honest naming — blasphemy and curse); Tobit 4:3 names the deathbed-instruction — *my son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life* (the second-Temple Yashar'el (Israel)-household's articulation of the all-the-days-of-her-life parental-honor extension). The framework reads the cluster as the wisdom-stream's direct corroboration of the Torah-substance the King defends against the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition. The Pharisaic-system had built the Corban-vow-mechanism to override the parental-honor commandment while preserving its righteousness-credentialing; the wisdom-stream had named the substance the tradition was voiding centuries before. The King's-charge at vv.3-6 lands at the same load-bearing diagnostic the wisdom-stream had named: the disposition that voids the parental-honor commandment is at the architecture of blasphemy-against-the-Torah-the-Father-spoke-from-Sinai.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother.* The King quotes the positive command (Shemot/Exodus 20:12) the Pharisaic Corban tradition voids.
*Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death* — Shemot (Exodus) 21:17's penalty-register the King quotes against the Corban-voiding.
